quizName: DMV Practice Test #13 40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: When another vehicle passes you, where should you ride in your lane?

options.text: In the left portion of your lane.
In the center portion of your lane.
In the right portion of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed, ride in the center of your lane. This is safest. Riding near the passing vehicle increases crash risk. Riding too far away may encourage the other driver to return to your lane too soon.

questions.question: Which part of the lane should you use when preparing to pass another vehicle on the left?
questions.correctAnswerText: The left portion
questions.explanation: Use the left portion of the lane when passing. This improves your view ahead and makes you more visible to oncoming traffic.

questions.question: When riding in a group, what does the lead rider mean by raising their left arm and pointing one finger, as shown in the image?

options.text: The group will exit at the next exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Form a single-file line.
questions.explanation: Hand signals help riders communicate in groups. When the lead rider raises their left arm and points one finger, all riders should form a single-file line.

questions.question: Riders without helmets are ________ to die in a crash than riders who wear helmets.
questions.correctAnswerText: Three times as likely
questions.explanation: Riders without helmets are three times more likely to die from head injuries in a crash than riders who wear helmets.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a cause of motorcycle wobbling?
questions.correctAnswerText: Uneven road
questions.explanation: Wobbles usually come from improper loading, unsuitable accessories, or incorrect tire pressure. Do not try to accelerate out of a wobble.

questions.question: A good lane position should do all of the following, EXCEPT:

options.text: Help you set up for turns.
Help you avoid wind from other vehicles.
Keep you in another vehicle's blind spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep you in another vehicle's blind spot.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see others and be seen. It helps you avoid wind, blind spots, and road hazards. It discourages other drivers from sharing your lane and gives you an escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: When entering a highway or taking a curve as a group, motorcyclists should:

options.text: Ride on the far right of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in a single-file line.
questions.explanation: Staggered formation is usually best for group riding. However, switch to single-file when turning, taking curves, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: When crossing railroad tracks that run parallel to the road, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Cross at about a 45-degree angle.
questions.explanation: To safely cross railroad tracks or road seams that run parallel to your lane, move to a position where you can cross at least at a 45-degree angle. Make a quick, sharp turn. If you cross slowly or at a small angle, the tracks could catch your tires and throw you off balance.

questions.question: In rain, where is it usually best to ride?

options.text: In the center of the lane.
Pull off the road until the rain stops.
In the tire tracks left by cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: When rain first starts, pavement is very slippery because car oil has not washed away yet. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars. The left tire track is often the best choice.

questions.question: Wobbling or shaking of the front wheel and handlebars can be caused by:

options.text: Brakes that do not work properly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Incorrect tire pressure.
questions.explanation: Wobbles usually come from improper loading, unsuitable accessories, or incorrect tire pressure.

questions.question: If you must swerve, what should you do?

options.text: Press the handlebar grip in the direction you want to turn.
Press the handlebar grip in the opposite direction of the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handlebar grip in the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: To swerve and avoid a hazard, press the handlebar grip in the direction you want to go. To swerve left, press the left grip, then the right to straighten out. To swerve right, press the right grip, then the left.

questions.question: As your motorcycle's weight moves forward while braking, what happens?

options.text: You can use more front brake pressure.
You should use less front brake pressure.
You can use more rear brake pressure.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can use more front brake pressure.
questions.explanation: When your weight shifts forward during braking, your front wheel gets more traction. This means you can apply the front brake harder.

questions.question: What is the correct way to swerve?

options.text: Press the handlebar grip in the direction you want to swerve.
Press the handlebar grip in the opposite direction of where you want to swerve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handlebar grip in the direction you want to swerve.
questions.explanation: To swerve and avoid a hazard, press the handlebar grip in the direction you want to go. To swerve left, press the left grip, then the right to straighten out. To swerve right, press the right grip, then the left.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, which is NOT something you should tell them to do?

options.text: Get on after the engine has started.
Sit as far forward as possible without crowding you.
Hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt.
Talk to you whenever they want.

questions.correctAnswerText: Talk to you whenever they want.
questions.explanation: Passengers should not distract the rider with unnecessary talk or movement. Passengers should board after the engine starts, sit forward without crowding you, and hold firmly to your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: If your front tire locks while braking, what should you do?

options.text: Release both brakes and coast to a stop.
Release the front brake and use only the rear brake.
Release the brake until the tire grips the road again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the brake until the tire grips the road again.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks while braking, release the brake lever until the tire regains grip. Then apply the brake again.

questions.question: How should a rider sit on a motorcycle for best control?

options.text: Using arms to hold up the body.
With knees away from the gas tank.
With feet firmly on the footrests.

questions.correctAnswerText: With feet firmly on the footrests.
questions.explanation: Sit so your arms control the motorcycle, not hold you up. Keep your arms slightly bent. Press your knees against the gas tank and keep your feet firmly on the footrests to maintain balance.

questions.question: What type of sign is rectangular?
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limit signs are rectangular with white backgrounds and black lettering. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders position themselves in a group?

options.text: At the back of the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Just behind the leader.
questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride just behind the leader. This lets experienced riders watch over them without making the new rider lead the group.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks while braking, what should you do?

options.text: Release the brake until the tire grips again, then re-apply it.
Release the brake and use only the front brake.
Keep the brake locked until you stop.
Release the brake and coast to a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the brake locked until you stop.
questions.explanation: If your rear wheel locks during braking, do not release the brake. Keep it locked until the motorcycle comes to a complete stop.

questions.question: How often should you check a motorcycle's hydraulic fluid at minimum?
questions.correctAnswerText: Once a week
questions.explanation: Check your hydraulic fluids and coolants at least once a week. Regular pre-ride inspections are important for safe riding.

questions.question: When riding through a curve, a group of motorcyclists should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in a single-file formation.
questions.explanation: Riders in a group should use a single-file formation when going through curves, making turns, entering a highway, or leaving a highway.

questions.question: The best way to brake in a straight line is by:

options.text: Using the front brake first, then the rear brake.
Using the rear brake first, then the front brake.
Using both brakes at the same time without locking either wheel.
Using both brakes at the same time while locking the rear wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using both brakes at the same time without locking either wheel.
questions.explanation: Use both the front and rear brakes at the same time to stop the best. Do not lock either wheel.

questions.question: Most motorcycle crashes happen:

options.text: After riding for a long time.

questions.correctAnswerText: On short trips.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen on short trips of less than five miles at speeds under 30 mph.

questions.question: Making eye contact with other drivers:

options.text: Guarantees they will yield to you.
Does not mean they see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not mean they see you.
questions.explanation: Do not rely on eye contact to know that a driver sees you. A driver can look directly at you and still not notice you.

questions.question: If you cannot avoid hitting an object in the road, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before contact.
questions.explanation: Slow down as much as you can before hitting the object. Keep your motorcycle upright. Rise slightly off the seat. Roll the throttle back a little just before impact.

questions.question: When being passed, do not move to the far side of your lane because:

options.text: The passing vehicle may return to your lane too soon.
You may block another vehicle from passing you.
The near side of the lane is safer.
You may feel a stronger wind blast from the passing vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: The passing vehicle may return to your lane too soon.
questions.explanation: Stay on the side of your lane closest to the passing vehicle. Moving to the far side may tempt the driver to return to your lane before it is safe.

questions.question: How does stopping distance for motorcycles compare to stopping distance for cars?

options.text: Cars need much longer to stop.
Cars need a little longer to stop.
Motorcycles and cars take about the same time to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycles and cars take about the same time to stop.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles and cars have nearly the same stopping distance under normal conditions. However, wet or slippery pavement makes stopping much harder for motorcycles.

questions.question: On a long trip, you should:

options.text: Take as few rest breaks as possible.
Use caffeine if you feel drowsy.
Dress warmly to stay comfortable during the ride.
Plan to ride more than 12 hours a day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Dress warmly to stay comfortable during the ride.
questions.explanation: Dress to protect yourself from wind, cold, and rain. Ride no more than six hours a day. Take a rest break at least every two hours. Do not use caffeine or other stimulants, as they cause extreme tiredness when they wear off.

questions.question: More than half of all motorcycle crashes:

options.text: Occur at speeds greater than 35 mph.
Involve riders with less than six months of experience on that motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Involve riders with less than six months of experience on that motorcycle.
questions.explanation: More than half of all motorcycle crashes involve riders who have had the motorcycle for less than six months.

questions.question: Small vehicles can appear ______ and seem to be traveling ______ than they actually are.
questions.correctAnswerText: Farther away, more slowly
questions.explanation: Motorcycles and other small vehicles look farther away and slower than they really are. This makes it hard for other drivers to judge their real distance and speed.

questions.question: How can you reduce your reaction time?

options.text: Ride slower than the speed limit.
Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
Shift into neutral when slowing down.
Pull in the clutch when turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
questions.explanation: Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes to reduce reaction time. This is especially helpful in areas where hazards are common.

questions.question: What happens to a sidecar during acceleration?

options.text: It feels like it is falling behind.
It feels like it is accelerating faster than the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: It feels like it is falling behind.
questions.explanation: A sidecar is an unpowered weight attached to your motorcycle. Due to its inertia, it will feel like it is falling behind when you accelerate.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders ride in a group?

options.text: At the front of the group.
At the back of the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Just behind the lead rider.
questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride near the front, just behind the leader. This lets experienced riders watch them from behind.

questions.question: How do motorcycle headlights compare to car headlights?

options.text: They are usually the same power.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are usually less powerful.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle headlights are smaller and less powerful than car headlights.

questions.question: What should you do when a vehicle passes you on your left?

options.text: Move as far right as possible to help them pass.
Move onto the shoulder to help them pass.
Stay in the center of your lane.
Move to the left side of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: Stay in the center of your lane when being passed. Moving toward the passing vehicle increases crash risk. Moving away from it may tempt them to merge back too soon. The center position is safest.

questions.question: What is the minimum following distance under normal conditions?
questions.correctAnswerText: Four seconds.
questions.explanation: Maintain at least four seconds of following distance under normal conditions. Increase this distance if conditions are not perfect.

questions.question: If you must both brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, what should you do?

options.text: Do one action first, then the other.
Do both at once and apply extra braking pressure.
Do both at once, but focus mainly on swerving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action first, then the other.
questions.explanation: Do not brake and swerve at the same time. You need full traction to swerve safely. Do one action first, then the other.

questions.question: How should you park a motorcycle next to a curb?

options.text: At a 90-degree angle with the rear wheel touching the curb.
At a 45-degree angle with the front tire touching the curb.
Like a car, with front and rear wheels the same distance from the curb.
At the left edge of the space so drivers can see it better.

questions.correctAnswerText: At a 90-degree angle with the rear wheel touching the curb.
questions.explanation: Park at a 90-degree angle to the curb with your rear wheel touching it.

questions.question: What should you do if a dog chases your motorcycle?

options.text: Stop until the animal loses interest.
Slow down as you approach, then speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down as you approach, then speed up.
questions.explanation: Downshift and approach the dog slowly. Then accelerate and leave it behind.

questions.question: Is the oily strip in the center of a lane safe for motorcycles?

options.text: Usually safe, unless the road is wet.
Usually safe, unless it is sunny outside.
Always safe, no matter the weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually safe, unless the road is wet.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars collects in a strip down the center of lanes. When the road is dry, this strip usually has enough traction for safe riding. When wet, avoid it. The strip is usually narrow enough that you can ride to one side and still stay in the center portion of your lane.
